done_when: When core.hooksPath is husky's folder, forge sync puts one line that runs Forge's pre-commit and pre-push checks (through .forge/hooks.sh) into the repo's committed .husky/pre-commit and .husky/pre-push, keeping their existing lines, and writes no shims into the folder husky rebuilds; the checks still run after npm install rebuilds that folder, in every worktree and a fresh clone; doctor reports the hooks installed in that setup; repos without husky keep today's shims; command tests cover a new husky repo and a husky repo adopted on an earlier release (including its earlier .pre-forge shims cleaned up)

findings.body: This previously reported gap remains open for both hooks. The generated line at src/forge/githooks.py:88–89 sources the launcher before calling forge_husky. Its PATH changes at src/forge/sync.py:78–81 therefore reach the user script launched here, overriding Husky's node_modules/.bin precedence (tests/fixtures/husky-v9.1.7/husky:16). An existing `eslint .` hook can run global ESLint instead of the repository's pinned executable. The isolation ruling covers exit/exec and stdin, but does not require changing command resolution. Preserve the incoming PATH for user checks and apply the launcher PATH only to Forge.
findings.title: Preserve Husky's PATH when running existing user hooks

findings.body: This previously reported gap remains open. An absolute core.hooksPath pointing to the original checkout's .husky/_ is detected successfully, but linked worktrees share that configuration and this guard rejects it there. Beyond the absolute-path detection ruling, the affected callers are verified: src/forge/upgrade.py:99 creates another checkout and line 146 runs sync there; src/forge/close.py:362–364 does the same for verification. Conflict inventory at src/forge/close.py:321–323 and oversized-fix inventory at src/forge/sync.py:369 also encounter the rejection. Consequently, this accepted configuration prevents upgrade and these close/commit workflows. Resolve the configuration explicitly for linked worktrees while retaining protection against writes outside the checkout.
findings.title: Handle absolute Husky paths during worktree-based upgrade and close

why: In client repos that use husky, every npm install rebuilds husky's hooks folder (core.hooksPath .husky/_) and wipes Forge's pre-commit and pre-push shims, so doctor reports the git hooks missing in every worktree after install (reported by a client session on v1.2.7). Owner decision 2026-10-08: add Forge to husky's own committed hooks
